### Day 112: Mark 1:29–30
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-112-mark-1-2930.html
Passage: Mark 1:29-30
Points:
- Christ does not remain confined to formal church spaces; He enters ordinary homes and families.
- People frequently wait for threatening life situations before urgently seeking the presence of Jesus.
- Jesus showed tender, personal care by drawing near and bending over the sick woman rather than healing from afar.
- Christ ministers directly to individuals who are completely powerless to help themselves.
- Homes today face relational and spiritual "fevers" that desperately require Christ's healing touch.

### Jesus Through Peter’s Mother-in-Law’s Eyes
Author: Rebecca McLaughlin
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/peter-mother-in-law/
Passage: Mark 1:29-31
Points:
- Peter's mother-in-law responds immediately to Jesus's touch by rising to serve, modeling the Christian life.
- In Christ's kingdom, serving reflects the example of Jesus Himself and is the calling of every believer.
- Grateful service leads to genuine human flourishing, whereas modern self-centered freedom often leads to misery.
- Jesus's healings reveal Him as the Isaiah 53 Suffering Servant who bears both our physical sickness and spiritual sin.
- Her immediate recovery gives believers a foretaste of the resurrection life where all suffering is banished.
